stem.en: A student says that sublimation is the same as evaporation, because both end in a vapour. Is the student right?

text.en: Yes. Both change a substance into vapour, so they are one process with two names.
No. Sublimation needs a flame, while evaporation can never use heat.
No. In sublimation a solid changes directly into vapour. In evaporation a liquid changes into vapour.
No. Evaporation leaves a solid on cool glass, and sublimation leaves a liquid.

explanation.en: Look at where each process starts. Sublimation starts from a solid and skips the liquid state, as camphor does. Evaporation starts from a liquid, as water in a wet cloth does. The student is right that both end in a vapour, which is why they seem alike, but the starting state is different. Heat can speed up either process, so a flame is not what separates them.

hints.en: What state does each process start from?
Think of camphor and of a wet cloth drying.
